text: Bahria Town (Private) Limited (Urdu: بحریہ ٹاؤن) is an Islamabad-based privately employee-owned real-estate development company that owns, develops, and manages properties across Pakistan. It established its first gated community in Rawalpindi/Islamabad and later launched its second in Lahore. In 2015, it launched Bahria Town Karachi, the largest of its gated communities, while Bahria Enclave Islamabad, launched in 2013, is the smallest. Most of these communities are large towns in their own right; the oldest community in the Southern Rawalpindi/Islamabad area spans over 16,000 hectares (40,000 acres), and the under-construction Bahria Town Karachi also spans over 16,000 hectares (40,000 acres), making it the largest privately owned residential community in the country. The company’s subsidiaries include the Mall of Lahore, the under-construction Mall of Islamabad, a chain of cinemas under the brand Cine Gold, a chain of supermarkets under the banner of Green Valley Hypermarket, and skyscrapers including the Bahria Icon Tower, the tallest building in Pakistan. The group is also the developer of the Grand Jamia Mosque in Lahore, the seventh largest mosque in the world with a total capacity of 70,000 people, and is constructing the third largest mosque in Karachi. The under-construction Rafi Cricket Stadium, when completed, will be the largest in the country. In November 2016, Bahria entered into a contract with Hyatt to develop four properties across Pakistan, including two golf resorts, worth a combined $600 million, with all properties owned by Bahria. ACE International Academy is also a project of Bahria Town. Bahria gated communities typically house upper-middle and high-income Pakistanis, feature private security, restrict access to non-residents, and are energy independent from the national grid. These communities include private schools operated by the company, private hospitals, hotels, and commercial avenues. Bahria has been featured by several international news agencies. Bahria Town Rawalpindi is the oldest and first project of Malik Riaz and is mostly located in Rawalpindi, sometimes referred to as Bahria Town Islamabad due to its partial location in the Islamabad Capital Territory. The original gated community has over 100,000 people and consists of multiple phases and smaller projects. Unlike other housing societies in Pakistan, Bahria produces its own electricity and sells it to residents through the Bahria Town Electric Supply Company, with Bahria Town projects in Rawalpindi and Lahore generating 12 and 9 megawatts respectively, and constructing three grid stations with its own resources while providing underground lines to residents. Bahria Enclave was launched in July 2011 and is located approximately 8 km from Chak Shahzad, the Park Road, and the Kuri Road, with access from Srinagar Highway, Lehtrar Road, and Islamabad Highway. On January 31, 2012, the Capital Development Authority approved the development of Jinnah Avenue in Zone-IV, a four-lane road linking main Kuri Road to Kuri Model Village, which was awarded to Bahria Town. Bahria Town Lahore is a flagship gated community in Lahore and is home to the Grand Jamia Mosque, Lahore, the seventh largest mosque in the world with a capacity of 70,000 people. Bahria Town Karachi is a privately developed, gated community located northeast of Karachi, along the M-9 Motorway, covering an area of 46,000 acres (72 sq mi; 19,000 ha), and is one of the largest private real estate developments in Pakistan, undertaken by the Bahria Town Group since 2014. Bahria Town Nawabshah is a currently constructed privately owned gated community in Benazirabad, Sindh, Pakistan, located at Qazi Abdullah Road on the bank of the Rohri Canal Nawabshah. On November 14, 2016, Hyatt Hotels Corporation and Bahria Town Group entered into an agreement in Abu Dhabi to develop four properties in Pakistan worth over $600 million, all of which were under construction as of 2016. After national success, Bahria has been featured by international magazines and news agencies, referred to as the prosperous face of Pakistan. GlobalPost reported in 2013 that Bahria houses some 100,000 people in total. Newsweek calls it Pakistan's "Gateway to Paradise," and on October 6, 2011, the Los Angeles Times referred to Bahria as a "functioning state within a non-functioning one." Despite this, Bahria has faced controversies and is referred to as a symbol of inequality, blamed for illegal encroachment of forests and unholy alliances with the military. The name 'Bahria' has been controversial, and in 2018, a senior court in Pakistan ruled against its use by private owners. Ayesha Siddiqa, a civilian military analyst and author of Military Inc.: Inside Pakistan's Military Economy, alleges that these links have enabled land acquisition, sometimes returning a percentage to senior officers as developed plots. Chief Executive of Bahria Town, Ali Riaz Malik, submitted a statement in the Supreme Court of Pakistan regarding the suo moto case involving Arsalan Iftikhar (son of Chief Justice Iftikhar Muhammad Chaudhry), asserting that Bahria Town was not behind any allegations and that the court proceedings were not aimed at investigating Bahria Town’s affairs. The written reply also stated that if any statement were made against Bahria Town or its administration, the organization would have the right to respond. In April 2016, Ahmed Ali Riaz Malik, son of Malik Riaz Hussain, was named in the Panama Papers. In August 2016, a resident complaint was forwarded to the Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP), revealing that Bahria Town deliberately prevented other fixed-line service providers from expanding into its communities, giving PTCL a majority market share and violating the Competition Act (2010) by abusing its dominant position and entering into a prohibited agreement. Six months later, CCP imposed a fine of 2 million PKR on Bahria Town for deliberately not issuing a NOC to Nayatel in Phases 1 to 6. Bahria Town has been directed to work with Nayatel to lay its fiber optic network in Phases 1 to 6.
